consequences: CC-010 can now require contextual-reference admission without choosing a second graph, runtime scheduler, cross-role bridge, or read-access policy.
CC-R06 retains production admission TDD, public diagnostics, and implementation against this closed design contract.
constraints: Every non-inlined Class-valued SlotUse is a strong graph reference. After the active general missing, null, presence, and cardinality pass, each surviving non-null scalar or multivalue member must resolve to an existing record of the declared class or subclass; mixin use alone is insufficient.

Admission visibility is accepted prestate plus earlier dependency-ordered candidate writes. Later, forward, same-create self, and cyclic references refuse the whole candidate and preserve pre-candidate state; runtime performs no topological sort or fixed-point search.

Every strong reference resolves in the same exact D06 admission role and replay-derived D07 partition. Cross-role and cross-partition targets refuse; primitive IDs and hashes outside Class-valued SlotUses remain scalar content.
Inlined Class values remain contained values and never enter contextual graph lookup.

Relation endpoints resolve to existing same-role and same-partition Entity records matching the declared endpoint class or subtype. Missing, wrong Entity type, Event, Signal, Relation, protocol, governance, cross-role, and cross-partition endpoints refuse.

Signal bearer remains an explicit same-role and same-partition contextual rule over an existing Entity or Relation. Missing, Event, Signal, cross-role, and cross-partition bearers refuse; bearer_id is not remodeled.

One global record-ID namespace remains across graph categories and partitions. Every selected temporal view must contain the target of each visible strong reference, endpoint, and bearer or refuse as structurally incomplete.

GraphRecipe dependency ordering remains compiler-side. The decision retains the existing one query surface and creates no read authorization, confidentiality, filtering, ACL, cascade, reverse-dependency inference, uncertainty propagation, interval proof, repair, migration, deletion, production, ontology, dependency, package, API, storage, or public diagnostic contract.
data.selected_option: Strong same-role and same-partition contextual references with Entity-only endpoints

summary: Accept strong same-role and same-partition contextual graph references with Entity-only endpoints.
why: The selected local-reference rule closes graph integrity with one visible admission context, one ID namespace, and referentially closed views. It preserves D06 role isolation, D07 partition topology, compiler-owned ordering, and KISS deferrals without inventing runtime scheduling, a second query surface, or implementation.
